summary: Intro discovery with Zenith Labs about migrating from OpenAI-hosted to Redwood Dedicated. Main concerns: latency/p95, cost parity, model behavior parity for safety filters, on-prem/VPC networking and KMS integration. Technical deep dive on vLLM/TGI compatibility, quantization, KV cache behavior, and benchmarking plan agreed.
transcript:
[00:00] Avery: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Avery from Redwood, AE on this account. quick roll call?
[00:08] Dana: Dana here, CTO at Zenith.
[00:11] Mark: Mark Chen, ML infra.
[00:14] Priya: Priya, infra ops.
[00:16] Samir: Samir Patel, solutions eng at Redwood.
[00:19] Lena: Lena, product, hi.
[00:22] Avery: Cool, agenda — understand current setup with OpenAI, latency/cost constraints, compatibility concerns (vLLM/TGI), and map out a benchmark and pilot. Is that right, Dana?
[00:31] Dana: Yes, that's right. We're exploring moving some high-volume endpoints off OpenAI due to cost and also to get better control of data residency. We also run some on-prem stuff for regulated customers.
[00:43] Mark: Technical context: we use OpenAI gpt-4o for chat and embeddings on a couple of routes. We also experimented with vLLM and TGI internally for inference to reduce cost but hit consistency issues with outputs and memory management. Majority of traffic is user-facing chat with p95 latency target ~400 ms, peak qps ~250.
[01:05] Samir: Got it. Quick clarifying q: when you say you tried vLLM/TGI, was that for the same model weights or a distilled variant?
[01:12] Mark: We tried both — FP16 on vLLM with LLM weights exported from the OpenAI-compatible checkpoints, and a trimmed TGI runtime for embeddings. The problem was sometimes the outputs drifted (eval delta) and kv cache behavior was buggy under load, we saw OOMs.
[01:30] Priya: Also network egress and data residency are concerns. We need to keep PII off third-party hosted unless contractually controlled. So private or dedicated with VPC peering and KMS is a must for the pilot.
[01:44] Avery: On the Dedicated side that's the exact use-case we see — dedicated GPU pools, VPC peering, KMS integration and audit logs. For eval parity, we run a parity suite to compare model outputs to your OpenAI baseline, we can include fuzz tests and safety filters.
[01:58] Dana: How close is parity usually? We need answers to match previous outputs for customer-facing flows; minor style differences ok but not hallucination regressions.
[02:07] Samir: Usually parity depends on model variant+quantization. If you stick to the same open checkpoint and use FP16/FP32 on equivalent kernels, parity is often high, like >95% on n-gram and rubric metrics, but quantized int8 or int4 can introduce differences. We can run A/B evals and flag regressions.
[02:28] Mark: We also need to understand latency — Redwood advertises low-latency, but for our set we need p95 under 400ms. What does Dedicated usually achieve?
[02:37] Samir: Typical p95 for Llama2-like 70B variants on a well-tuned Dedicated pod is in the ~200-500ms range depending on sequence length. With batching and KV cache, conversational flows get much better after warmup. We can tune batching windows and target p95 with autoscaling.
[02:53] Priya: Warmup and KV cache — you mentioned KV cache; earlier our vLLM runs had inconsistent KV cache reuse across sessions, leading to latency spikes. How stable is Redwood's KV management?
[03:05] Samir: We do continuous KV cache management with sticky routing for sessions and automatic prefix caching. There are corner cases though — if you have user-level isolation and rotate models, cache misses happen. We'll include cache hit rate metrics in the observability dashboard.
[03:19] Dana: Security checklist — SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs, RBAC — can you share docs?
[03:25] Avery: Yes, we'll send the security pack after the call (SOC2 report, encryption docs, SSO/SAML flow, RBAC examples).
[03:31] Lena: On the business side, pricing — what's the delta between hosted OpenAI-like pricing and Redwood Dedicated? We need ballpark to decide if migration makes sense.
[03:40] Avery: Dedicated is commit-based. For your QPS and usage profile, the unit costs are generally lower at scale vs public API, but there is a monthly reserved capacity charge. We'll send a modeled pricing sheet for your throughput.
[03:51] Mark: One more technical: model compatibility with OpenAI API — do you support function calling and chat schema parity?
[03:58] Samir: We support chat and structured outputs; function-calling patterns can be mapped. There are slight API differences; we provide an adapter and an SDK shim to minimize application changes. We also have a migration checklist for prompt/response normalization.
[04:12] Dana: For on-prem, how much of the control plane remains with Redwood? We need to keep control plane local for compliance.
[04:19] Samir: Private deployments can be customer-managed control plane or hybrid. For fully air-gapped we ship an on-prem package. For VPC we host the control plane but provide private networking and audit logs. We'll detail the tradeoffs in the docs.
[04:31] Mark: Regarding benchmarks — what do you need from us to run a realistic parity and performance benchmark?
[04:36] Samir: Ideally: representative prompt sets (typical chat sessions and worst-case long context tests), target SLOs for p95 and throughput, a sample of embeddings workload if any, and any safety filters or post-processing you run. We will run a baseline against your OpenAI traffic for output comparison and measure latency on Dedicated hardware.
[04:55] Priya: We'll put that together. Our ops concern is network egress and key management — can Redwood integrate with our AWS KMS and existing IAM roles?
[05:03] Samir: Yes — we support AWS KMS, and HSM integrations for Private. For Dedicated we can integrate with customer KMS via VPC endpoints or bring-your-own-key. We'll include a diagram.
[05:16] Dana: Revocation and audit — do you maintain token-level tracing and full request logs?
[05:22] Avery: Yes, the Console exposes token-level cost/latency breakdowns and per-request tracing hooks. For Private/Dedicated we can set retention policies.
[05:30] Mark: About model variants — we currently use gpt-4o, will Redwood run something equivalent? Are there recommended open checkpoints?
[05:38] Samir: We onboard open models and curated variants. For gpt-4o-like workloads we recommend tuned Llama3/Starcoder hybrids depending on task. We'll propose model candidates and run eval parity to pick the best fit.
[05:50] Lena: Any known incompatibilities with TGI runtimes — we saw some tokenization mismatch.
[05:55] Samir: Tokenization mismatches often come from different tokenizer versions or pre/post processing. We have tokenizer adapters and explicit tokenization checks in the migration checklist.
[06:04] Dana: What about quantization? We tried int8 and saw hallucination increase.
[06:09] Samir: Quantization tradeoffs are real. int8/int4 lowers cost significantly; however eval drift needs to be measured. For customer-facing flows we often recommend FP16 with selective quantization for low-risk routes, or run shadow quantized models and compare.
[06:24] Mark: For the benchmark, can Redwood run both quantized and FP16 variants and provide output diffs?
[06:29] Samir: Yes, we'll run both and include automated diff summaries and a regression dashboard.
[06:35] Priya: Networking question: VPC peering with our prod VPC — is there a documented runbook?
[06:40] Avery: Yes, we have runbooks for VPC peering, private endpoints, and peered cross-account roles. We'll attach the network diagram.
[06:48] Dana: For our compliance team, they will want to review SOC2 and encryption in detail.
[06:53] Avery: We'll send SOC2, encryption, and a sample dataplane architecture.
[06:57] Mark: Can Redwood support canary deploys and model rollbacks?
[07:02] Samir: Yes — rollouts, canary, A/B tests, automatic fallback to baseline model are supported in the Console.
[07:10] Lena: Do you provide event hooks or webhooks for inference completion?
[07:14] Samir: Yes, async webhook and streaming support for responses.
[07:18] Dana: On cost — if we move embeddings to Dedicated, how much savings could we expect versus OpenAI embeddings?
[07:25] Avery: It depends on commit size; often significant at tens of millions of embeddings per month. We'll model your numbers in the pricing sheet.
[07:33] Mark: Operationally, we need a clear rollback plan in case outputs diverge in prod.
[07:38] Samir: We recommend a staged rollout: shadow run, A/B with scoring, then canary, with automatic fallback policy that sends traffic back to OpenAI or a baseline variant if regression thresholds trigger.
[07:51] Dana: Ok, next steps from our side: we'll collate sample prompts and SLOs. From Redwood: pricing and security docs and benchmark plan.
[07:59] Avery: Perfect. Samir, can you own the benchmark plan?
[08:03] Samir: Yep, I'll own it. I'll propose time windows and required artifacts by tomorrow.
[08:09] Mark: Quick question on SLA for Dedicated — what's the uptime SLA?
[08:13] Avery: Dedicated has SLA options, typically 99.9% with higher tiers available. We'll include specifics in the SOW.
[08:20] Priya: Anything we should be aware of for the pilot's timeline? We want pilot running in about 4 weeks.
[08:26] Samir: 4 weeks is doable if artifacts are provided promptly — sample prompts, traffic shape, and infra approvals for VPC peering.
[08:35] Dana: Any blockers from Redwood's side?
[08:38] Avery: No major blockers. We'll need the sample data and a primary contact for infra to provision peering.
[08:45] Lena: Let's recap next steps aloud.
[08:47] Avery: Recap: Redwood send security pack and pricing (Avery), Samir run benchmark plan and schedule, Zenith to share prompt sets and SLOs (Mark/Dana), follow-up demo week of 4/27.
[09:02] Dana: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[09:05] Samir: Thanks all. We'll follow up with calendar invites and the benchmark plan.
[09:10] Avery: Endcall.
